_meta.description: Curated author attributions for whole-volume / anthology corpus keys (ocr.*, cogPG.*) that build_registry.py's ingested-works pass would otherwise file under a pseudo-author minted from the slug prefix (anon-ocr, anon-cogPG). Each work entry names the real author slug (reusing the canon author entry when one exists), a display title, and the two evidence sources used to verify the attribution: (1) the volume's own served rows in data/corpus/<key>.jsonl (incipits, section heads, and token shares measured by cumulative position), and (2) the standard bibliography for the volume (the Patrologia Graeca per-volume table; the edition's own title for Walz / Mansi / Bussemaker-Daremberg). Multi-author volumes are attributed to the dominant author only when that author holds >=90% of the served tokens; otherwise a collective label naming the actual authors is used. Per-treatise dissolution of the collective volumes is future work.

policy.dominant_author: attribute to an author holding >=90% of served tokens (share documented)
policy.collective: no author reaches 90%: mint a name-only collective label naming the actual authors
policy.qids: every real-person author entry carries a Wikidata QID verified against wikidata.org (dates/description); collective labels and editions without a Wikidata item stay name-only

rhetores-graeci-walz.note: Collective label for Christian Walz's nine-volume anthology Rhetores Graeci (Stuttgart/Tuebingen 1832-1836). No Wikidata item exists for the collection itself (checked 2026-07-10); per-treatise attribution (Hermogenes, Aphthonius, Sopatros, Doxopatres, Psellus, ...) is a future dissolution.

Served shares: Isidore of Thessalonica (Glabas) sermons on the Theotokos ~0-17%, Joel Chronographia compendiaria ~17-24%, Nicetas Choniates (Historia incl. De statuis/post-1204 section at 90.7%, Thesaurus head at tail) ~76%. Choniates dominant but below 90%.

palamas-acindynus-barlaam-pg151.name: Gregorius Palamas, Acindynus et Barlaam (PG 151)
palamas-acindynus-barlaam-pg151.note: Collective for what REMAINS of PG 151 after the 2026-08-07 per-work carve (issue #8), which is no longer the whole volume. Palamas' homiliary (10-282) and Philotheus' encomium (283-346) and antirrhetics (394-576) are now served under their own slugs; the residual is 347-393, the synodal dossier of the hesychast controversy, plus two anonymous treatises at 577-600 and 603-628. All three men named in this label appear throughout the dossier (Akindynos on 21 pages, Palamas on 8, Barlaam on 4) but as PARTIES to it, not as its authors: it is the tome, Cantacuzenus' prostagma and the bishops' report. The label is kept collective for that reason, and no century is asserted, since a dossier and two unattributed treatises do not share one.

dionysius-pachymeres-pg3.name: Pseudo-Dionysius Areopagita et Georgius Pachymeres (PG 3)
dionysius-pachymeres-pg3.note: Collective for PG 3, which Migne prints as the Corpus Dionysiacum WITH Pachymeres' paraphrase interleaved, not as Dionysius alone. Served shares: Pseudo-Dionysius 60,010 of 160,260 tokens, about 37%, taking the vendored canon's word counts for the five works (CH 11,488, EH 16,400, DN 24,104, MT 1,350, Ep 6,668); the remaining ~63% is Georgius Pachymeres' 13th-century paraphrase. Neither reaches the 90% this file's policy requires for a dominant-author attribution.

euthalius-diaconus.name: Euthalius Diaconus
euthalius-diaconus.note: Euthalius the Deacon, credited by the manuscript tradition with the prologue, travel summary and martyrdom notice that accompany Paul's epistles. Migne prints three of those with their own Greek heads in the Oecumenius volume (PG118). The vendored TLG Canon has no entry for him, so these works carry no external anchor.

cogPG.PG003.author: dionysius-pachymeres-pg3
cogPG.PG003.title: Patrologia Graeca 3
cogPG.PG003.attribution: collective (Pseudo-Dionysius ~37% of served tokens, Pachymeres' paraphrase ~63%, no author reaches 90%)
evidence: measured: 160,260 served tokens by the corpus tokenizer against 60,010 words for the five Dionysian works in data/inventory/work_inventory.json (tlg2798.001, .002, .004, .005, .006), so Dionysius holds about 37% and cannot take the volume under this file's >=90% dominant-author rule

PG 3's own title page prints the text cum paraphrasi Pachymerae; the paraphrase is interleaved with the text rather than segregated, which is why the volume cannot be split by column and is tracked in issue #9

century tag deliberately absent: the two authors are about 700 years apart, so any single value misdates the majority of the volume. The other PG collectives keep a century because their authors sit in one period; this is the Walz-anthology case, where contents straddle periods and no century is asserted

previous attribution was 'single-author volume' under pseudo-dionysius-areopagita with century 6, which dated roughly 100,000 tokens of 13th-century paraphrase to the 6th and broke the policy stated in this file's own _meta

nicolaus-rhetoric.progymnasmata-walz-i-2.author: nicolaus-rhetoric
nicolaus-rhetoric.progymnasmata-walz-i-2.title: Progymnasmata (paradigmata, Walz I 263-420)
nicolaus-rhetoric.progymnasmata-walz-i-2.attribution: named in the printed title and defended by the editor
evidence: Walz, Rhetores Graeci I, printed 263: ΝΙΚΟΛΑΟΥ ΣΟΦΙΣΤΟΥ ΠΡΟΓΥΜΝΑΣΜΑΤΑ, no qualifier; every verso running head across 263-420 reads ΝΙΚΟΛΑΟΥ; the volume's contents entry is a bare Νικολάου προγυμνάσματα in a list where Walz writes Ἀνωνύμου for the anonymous items

Walz at printed 265 defends the ascription against Schoell, citing the authority of Par. 2918; at 264 he says what he prints are the paradigmata from that manuscript and that Nicolaus' theoria is a separate work he has not found

Felten, praefatio to the 1913 Teubner Progymnasmata, from the other side: in codicibus Nicolao tribuuntur exempla, Μελέται Suidae, quae praecepta illa illustrant (cf. Walz I 266 sq.), sed qui nexus huic Nicolao cum illis intercedat, nondum constat

NOT the same work as the served nicolaus-rhetoric.progymnasmata: word-bigram containment 0.123 against it, where the genuine other edition (Spengel III) scores 0.720 and unrelated progymnasmata of the same genre land at 0.11-0.17. Do not merge the two on the strength of their shared title.
